title: Video assistant referee
summary:
This document provides a comprehensive overview of the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system in association football. It begins by defining the roles of VAR officials, including the assistant video assistant referees (AVARs) and replay operators, before detailing the operational procedures—covering the four categories of reviewable decisions (goals, penalties, direct red cards, and mistaken identity), the checking process, and the on-field review (OFR) protocol. The document also explains offences related to the VAR process, the location of VAR teams (including centralized review hubs), and the camera setup, followed by a glossary of technical terms and abbreviations.

The historical section traces VAR's development from an early pioneering use in Yemen in 2006, through its conception under the Royal Netherlands Football Association's Refereeing 2.0 project, its initial trials in the Eredivisie, and its formal incorporation into the Laws of the Game by IFAB in March 2018. It chronicles VAR's first deployments in various competitions worldwide, including Dutch cup matches, the A-League, Major League Soccer, the FIFA Confederations Cup, and top European leagues, as well as its eventual adoption by the Premier League and UEFA Champions League.

Notable applications of VAR are examined through the 2018 and 2026 FIFA World Cups, highlighting key decisions, controversies, statistical impacts, and rule changes such as the "mistaken identity" review. Finally, the document addresses issues and criticisms of VAR, including technical malfunctions, miscommunication errors, lack of transparency, subjective decision inconsistencies, increased match delays, effects on fan experience, injury risks from delayed offside calls, and recent technological improvements like semi-automated offside technology.
